# Leave a trail {#trail background-color="#f0674d"}

Make a project something a co-author could rerun. Practice on a messy one, then do
one of your own.

## The folder {#folder}

A paper you're writing with Kari Nordmann: *Monthly or yearly? Price framing and
willingness to pay.* A survey experiment, cleaned in Excel, written up in Word.
Fictional, and completely typical.

Start the agent in an empty folder, and paste the **download prompt from the
handout, section 8**. (Or unzip `practice/messy-project.zip` from the course files
yourself.)

## What's in it

```
messy-project/
├── survey_export_2026-03-14.csv    the raw survey, 240 rows
├── data_clean_FINAL.csv            cleaned by hand in Excel
├── analysis.py                     first try
├── analysis_v2.py                  the analysis
├── table1.txt                      results
├── table1 (copy).txt               results?
├── notes.txt                       "the crazy WTP ones?? ask Kari"
└── draft_v3.docx                   the Word draft
```

Could Kari rerun this? Could you, next spring?

## Why text

| | Invisible | Visible |
|---|---|---|
| **Writing** | Word: you can't see what changed | Text: every change shows |
| **Data** | Clicking in Excel: no record | A script: the steps are the record |

- The agent reads and writes text, and so can you, in Notepad.
- Writing in LaTeX? That's text already.
- Writing in Word? Keep Word for the paper. Keep the rest in text, and ask for a
  Word copy when you need one.

## Reinhart and Rogoff (2010) {#rr}

[−0.1% → +2.2%]{style="font-size: 2.2em; font-weight: 800; color: #f0674d;"}

Average growth when public debt is above 90% of GDP: as published, and after a
grad student redid it from their spreadsheet in 2013.

- Part of it: an `AVERAGE` over rows 30–44, not 30–49. Five countries left out.
- The rest: years left out, and how the countries were weighted.

> Your own rerun finds it first.

## Exercise: organise it

1. *"Set up git here and commit everything."* Same move as this morning.
2. *"Organise this folder so a co-author could rerun everything. Show me the plan
   first. Don't move anything yet."*
3. Argue with the plan. Then let it run.
4. *"Write a README for a co-author, and a project file for you."* Then *"Commit."*

## The test {#test}

```{=html}
{{< include images/rerun-test.svg >}}
```

::: {.prompt}
Rerun everything from scratch. Do you get the same numbers?
:::

## What the rerun found {#found}

The practice folder was cleaned **by hand in Excel**, with two rules. Drop the
speeders: written down. Drop three answers above 5,000 NOK: **not written down.**

| | N | Effect | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep the three | 223 | −292 NOK | 0.26 |
| Drop them | 220 | +53 NOK | 0.02 |

An undocumented click in Excel decided the sign of the result. The rerun test found it.

> A wrong script you can read beats a right click you can't remember.

- Copy a real project folder, or take this morning's paper folder. Work on the copy.
